primitives.name: Dependent Pairwise Likelihood Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Novel contribution: for the dependent-data Thurstone model Z_s = A T + e_s with T ~ N(μ, Σ_T) inducing correlation across a subject's comparisons, estimation by pairwise likelihood (product of bivariate marginal likelihoods over comparison pairs) instead of the full 6-dimensional (for n=4 objects) likelihood.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Z_s': 'latent comparison vector for subject s, dimension 6', 'T': 'latent trait vector, N(μ, Σ_T)', 'A': 'design matrix mapping traits to comparisons', 'e_s': 'error term, N(0, ω^2 I_6)', 'θ': 'model parameters'}
primitives.assumptions: Bivariate marginals correctly specified, subjects independent, comparison graph connected
primitives.breakdown_regime: When comparison graph is disconnected or marginals mis-specified

layer2.mapping: Enables scalable inference for correlated analyst judgments in GSE's matchup aggregation pipeline
layer2.telemetry: Coverage probability of Wald confidence intervals

primitives.name: Thurstone Normal Cumulative Distribution Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Mathematics/equations/assumptions - Thurstone: P(i beats j) = Φ(μ_i - μ_j); Bradley–Terry: P(i beats j) = exp(λ_i)/(exp(λ_i)+exp(λ_j)); identification μ_4 = 0.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Φ': 'standard normal cumulative distribution function', 'μ_i': 'latent worth of item i, dimensionless', 'μ_4': 'reference item worth, set to zero for identifiability'}
primitives.assumptions: Normality of latent traits, transitivity of preferences
primitives.breakdown_regime: When preferences are not transitive or latent traits deviate from normality

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's probabilistic ranking framework for comparative evaluation
layer2.telemetry: Rank correlation between predicted and observed outcomes

primitives.name: Bradley-Terry Logistic Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Mathematics/equations/assumptions - Thurstone: P(i beats j) = Φ(μ_i - μ_j); Bradley–Terry: P(i beats j) = exp(λ_i)/(exp(λ_i)+exp(λ_j)); identification μ_4 = 0.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'λ_i': 'logit-scale worth of item i, dimensionless', 'λ_4': 'reference item logit worth, set to zero for identifiability'}
primitives.assumptions: Independence of irrelevant alternatives, additive logit structure
primitives.breakdown_regime: When preferences violate IIA or when data is sparse

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in replacing full likelihood with pairwise likelihood for dependent data, enabling tractable inference in high-dimensional settings. The Thurstone model assumes normally distributed latent traits, while Bradley-Terry uses logistic link functions. Both are unified under a common framework where pairwise likelihood approximates full ML with near-nominal coverage. The dependent-data extension introduces a multivariate normal latent trait vector T with covariance Σ_T, capturing inter-subject correlations. Pairwise likelihood simplifies computation by focusing on bivariate marginals, avoiding the need for 6D integrals. Sandwich standard errors ensure valid inference even under misspecification. In GSE, this supports robust aggregation of repeated analyst judgments and correlated player comparisons. The key insight is that dependence can be modeled without full likelihood, preserving computational feasibility and statistical validity.
